articles.proposed_title: Checking Recalls on an Imported Used Car: What a UK Buyer Should Confirm Before Paying
articles.primary_query: imported used car recall check UK VIN
articles.search_intent: Confirm outstanding safety campaigns and documented remedy status for an imported used car before payment, accounting for database coverage limits.
articles.buyer_task: Collect the correct identity and original-market details, use applicable official/manufacturer checks, and request campaign/remedy evidence before accepting an unclear result.
articles.target_buyer: UK importer or small-fleet procurement manager

sources.title: Check if a vehicle, part or accessory has been recalled

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: UK guidance provides registration-based recall checking and a make/model/manufacture-year route when registration is unknown.
sources.limitations: Do not equate a model-level notice with a particular VIN's repair-completion status.

sources.title: Recalled vehicles, parts and accessories

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Manufacturer notices explain the reason, next action and contact; notification depends on having the owner's contact details.
sources.limitations: Do not promise receipt of a letter, universally free overseas repairs or a universal stop-driving instruction.

sources.title: Product recalls and updates

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Honda explicitly warns that European records may not show an imported vehicle's outstanding recall or update and directs owners to Honda/dealers.
sources.limitations: Honda-specific example only. Static form text contains contradictory result placeholders; no VIN was submitted and no vehicle result was obtained.

sources.title: Toyota Recalls

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Toyota provides recall checking and dealer contact for current and previous campaigns.
sources.limitations: Toyota-specific process. Do not extrapolate UK service arrangements or remedy availability to every imported vehicle or destination.

sources.title: Owners FAQs

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Volkswagen directs customers to its retailer and identifies UK registration as a condition of the government outstanding-recall route described in its FAQ.
sources.limitations: Volkswagen UK process only; no particular campaign, VIN, vehicle age or repair price is asserted.

sources.title: Vehicle Recalls

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Its VIN service depends on manufacturer participation; it directs users to the manufacturer/dealer when a make is absent.
sources.limitations: Industry service explanation, not a statute or proof that a vehicle is recall-free. No form, terms or CAPTCHA was submitted.

articles.intended_distinction: Campaign lookup coverage and remedy evidence, rather than software localisation, shipping acceptance or general VIN/photo inspection.
blocked_facts: Every brand's UK database covers all grey imports
A model-level match establishes VIN applicability
Universal cross-border free repair or warranty entitlement
Blanket stop-driving rule for every recall

articles.proposed_title: Before Ordering EVs for a UK Small Fleet: Check AC Limits, Supply Phases and Overnight Charging
articles.primary_query: UK small fleet AC onboard charger single three phase depot
articles.search_intent: Match an already-compatible vehicle's onboard AC capability and overnight operating needs to a UK small-business site's available supply before placing a fleet order.
articles.buyer_task: Ask for exact-market vehicle AC specifications and a site assessment, distinguish vehicle/chargepoint/supply constraints, and identify evidence needed before ordering.
articles.target_buyer: UK importer or small-fleet procurement manager

sources.title: Charging your business's electric vehicles

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Depot planning should consider overnight dwell time, electricity supply and the vehicle's AC charging limit.
sources.limitations: The page includes old electricity prices, simplified charging-time arithmetic and inconsistent kWh/kW wording. Exclude these numerical examples and cost claims.

sources.title: Types of chargers

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: AC charging uses the onboard charger; DC supplies the battery through a different charging path.
sources.limitations: Explain the architecture only; do not transfer illustrative charging curves or hours to a specific vehicle.

sources.title: DNO connection scenarios

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: Infrastructure planning distinguishes connection capacity, phases, equipment power and future demand; its table gives three-phase examples for higher-power AC charging.
sources.limitations: Planning examples, not an installation design or a guaranteed DNO offer. Do not generalise SSEN thresholds to every DNO.

sources.title: Why EVs may reach 11kW despite zappi's 22kW capability

scope.model_year: N/A — process guide, no model specifications

sources.supported_fact_candidate: The equipment manufacturer's explanation distinguishes its chargepoint rating from the vehicle's onboard AC limit.
sources.limitations: Primary for its own product behaviour only. 'Many EVs' is not evidence of any selected model's specification; do not repeat promotional suitability claims.
